CHIEF COMPLAINT
Follow-up visit to evaluate the management of anxiety, sleep disturbances, persistent fatigue, and headache symptoms, with a focus on recent changes in symptomatology.
HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mr. John Smith returns for his follow-up appointment, expressing notable fluctuations in his symptoms over the past month. He reports that while his sleep onset has slightly improved, he continues to struggle with early morning awakenings, particularly during the workweek, where he averages only 5-6 hours of sleep. He attributes this ongoing issue to heightened anxiety regarding impending project deadlines and workplace pressures. The trazodone at 75 mg remains beneficial for nocturnal awakenings, but he is increasingly frustrated by his inability to sustain sleep through the night.
In terms of fatigue, Mr. Smith notes that while his energy levels have improved slightly, he still experiences significant exhaustion during high-stress periods. He describes his fatigue as both physical and mental, particularly exacerbated by long hours at work. He continues to report headaches, which have increased in frequency to 3-4 times per week, with an intensity of 5-7 out of 10. He is using ibuprofen 400 mg more frequently, approximately 4 times weekly, and expresses concern regarding the potential for gastrointestinal side effects from increased usage.
Mr. Smith remains committed to his holistic treatment plan, including regular acupuncture sessions and participation in yoga classes. He finds cognitive-behavioral therapy sessions helpful, particularly in developing strategies to manage anxiety and stress, but feels that he may need to intensify his therapy sessions given the recent exacerbation of symptoms.
PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder - diagnosed in 2021 2. Insomnia - diagnosed in 2021 3. Tension-Type Headaches - diagnosed in 2021 4. Hypertension - diagnosed in 2020, currently well-controlled on lisinopril 10 mg daily
MEDICATIONS
1. Sertraline 200 mg daily 2. Trazodone 75 mg at bedtime 3. Melatonin 10 mg at bedtime 4. Lisinopril 10 mg daily 5. Ibuprofen 400 mg as needed for headache relief (increased usage) 6. Amitriptyline 40 mg nightly 7. Topiramate 25 mg daily (continue current dosage) 8. Lorazepam 0.5 mg as needed (continued reduced dosage)
ALLERGIES
No known drug allergies.
SOCIAL HISTORY
Mr. Smith continues to work as a software engineer, where he reports that project deadlines remain a significant source of stress. He has been actively engaging in yoga and meditation practices, which he finds beneficial for managing stress levels. He abstains from alcohol and maintains a primarily plant-based diet, with an emphasis on whole foods and reduced processed food intake.
REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
- Psychiatric: Sleep initiation difficulties persist, particularly on work nights; anxiety has worsened with increased stress; no suicidal ideation or depressive symptoms reported. - Neurological: Headache frequency has increased; intensity fluctuates; no visual changes or neurological deficits. - Cardiovascular: No chest pain, palpitations, or dyspnea. - General: Persistent fatigue; no fever or significant weight changes.
PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
- Vital Signs: BP 120/76 mmHg, HR 74 bpm, RR 16 breaths/min, Temp 98.6F - General: Alert, oriented, and appears fatigued but in no acute distress. - Neurological: Cranial nerves II-XII intact; no motor or sensory deficits observed. - Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm; no murmurs or gallops. - Psychiatric: Cooperative; maintains good eye contact; mood appears stable but fatigued.
ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Generalized Anxiety Disorder: Continue sertraline at 200 mg daily. Given the increased anxiety levels, recommend increasing lorazepam to 1 mg as needed during peak stress periods and encourage more frequent cognitive-behavioral therapy sessions. 2. Insomnia: Maintain trazodone at 75 mg; continue melatonin at 10 mg. Discuss the possibility of introducing a sleep study if sleep onset and maintenance difficulties persist. 3. Tension-Type Headaches: Continue amitriptyline at 40 mg nightly. Given the increased headache frequency, consider increasing topiramate to 50 mg daily and reassess in the next visit. 4. Persistent Fatigue: Encourage continued engagement in physical activity and mindfulness practices. Continue working with the nutritionist for dietary optimization and explore alternative therapies or referrals to specialists if fatigue persists.
Follow-up appointment scheduled for 2028-12-01 to evaluate ongoing symptoms, assess treatment efficacy, and make further medication adjustments as necessary. Mr. Smith is advised to contact the office sooner if he experiences any exacerbation of symptoms or adverse effects from medications.
